- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to prior trend.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+10% from 10-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high or 10% below recent 5-day high.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.3), model underestimates mean reversion — adjust downward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days to align with historical mean reversion speed.
- When sentiment turns positive after negative phase, model delays reaction — forecast should start rising 1–2 days earlier than sentiment suggests.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in cycle (first 5–7 days) — apply 3–5% downward bias to first 7 days of forecast.
- If sentiment shows strong divergence from price trend (e.g., sentiment +0.5 while price falls), model often ignores sentiment — reduce forecast by 5–10% if sentiment > 0.3 and price is falling.
